title.narrative: An up-to-date skills needs anticipation system for reducing skills mismatches and enhancing access to the labour market in place

description.narrative: A key concern for constituents in North Macedonia is workforce employability. However, there is limited access to detailed and relevant information on skills needs, mismatches and forecasting, and existing data is not effectively translated into training programmes. The country’s economic development strategy does not integrate skills development as a driver of productivity and competitiveness, creating a disconnect between economic growth needs, labour market demands and the education system. An OECD (2022) assessment on SME policies highlights progress in supporting SMEs through improved access to finance, innovation, and internationalization. However, it calls for greater efforts in entrepreneurial learning and enterprise skills. While the Ministry of Labour and employers’ organizations frequently raise concerns about skills mismatches, there is a lack of strategic initiatives to align economic growth with workforce development, particularly in sectors with high employment potential or productivity gains. To address these gaps, the ILO is seeking to support skills needs anticipation to help identify future workforce demands and establish priorities for skills development in growth sectors. This will raise awareness and strengthen capacities to connect skills development with enterprise needs. The findings will inform TVET planning, curriculum development, and career guidance. Complementary to the efforts on skills development the ILO is also looking into the insertion of entrepreneurship education into TVET and secondary and tertiary education, as well as enhancing the provision of financial and non-financial services for SMEs. These efforts aim to reduce skills mismatches and enhance youth employability and workforce productivity at the sectoral level.
